prize_parts.citation: for theories of firm heterogeneity and selection in trade, showing how exporting decisions and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My preferred part and laureate pair are unchanged from round 1. What changed is the framing of the citation and my alternatives. I now word the citation around the theoretical mechanism, selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and reallocation across firms, and not around the empirical exporter facts. That is the claim I actually hold, so I give up nothing by wording it this way, which answers the chair's question to B044 supporters. The case is the same on three counts. First, there is one originating model (Melitz 2003) and one natural complement (Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus foreign direct investment). Second, more than twenty years of firm-level evidence from many countries has confirmed the qualitative predictions on selection, the extensive margin and reallocation, and the dispute is about welfare magnitudes and not about whether the mechanism exists. Third, it is a distinct later advance on the scale and variety mechanisms recognised in 2008. On the chair's question about neighbouring prizes, I would count adjacency against a candidate only when the earlier citation covered the same discovery. A past prize is not a quota. If it were applied as a quota it would bear on B044 (2008), B038 (2021, 2023, 2024), B037 (2022) and B017 (2024) alike. The pair also keeps the whole configuration at two people, well inside the three-person cap. I make this case from the mechanism, its attribution and its maturity. The fact that five of eleven round-1 files named this part is not evidence of merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution. Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum made closely related empirical and quantitative contributions, and Redding's later quantitative extensions are real. A two-name award would leave parts of the field uncredited, and I cannot make that go away. Welfare magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions (Pareto productivity, CES demand), so the quantitative gains from trade are model-dependent even where the qualitative mechanism is solid. Trade was recognised in 2008, and some members will weigh that against a second trade prize. The B044 support so far is five of eleven, short of the six needed, and B038 and B037 are serious rivals on importance. Because I work in industrial organisation and trade, I may also be over-reading the clarity of the Melitz credit boundary. A related caution is that the strongest empirical support for B044 is firm-level trade data, which is my own field's evidence base.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B037 first with Kiyotaki and Moore as the clean originators. He lists B044 as his first alternative but says the missing empirical pioneers (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) keep him from placing it first, and he cannot resolve that boundary from the supplied evidence.
responses.response: I agree that B037 has the cleaner attribution, and I ranked it second myself. The collateral-value mechanism is distinct from the bank-run and intermediation results recognised in 2022. On your attribution concern for B044, my answer is that the Eaton-Kortum work is a Ricardian strand and not the selection mechanism. The Bernard-Jensen exporter facts motivated the theory but do not replace the integrated model. If the citation names the theory of selection and the gains from trade, the exclusion is defensible, though not free of dispute. I still do not make B037 my preferred part, because the support for the collateral channel is largely model-based. If B044 cannot reach six votes, B037 remains one of my two fallbacks, so your disclosed preference for it does not change my view of its merit.

responses.point: Andersson moved B038 to first with Autor, Hanson and Katz. He cites my round-1 Autor-Hanson proposal, agrees that the strands should not be blurred, and says Autor and Hanson is a fallback he could accept, but argues that dropping Katz leaves the citation resting on the more contested trade-shock magnitudes.
responses.response: That is a fair account of my opening position, and the reasoning that Katz anchors the older technology and wage-structure strand has moved me part of the way. I still read the strands as separable, so the choice is between a trade-shock-and-local-labour-market award and a broader labour-demand award. I would not rule out either, but I cannot say the evidence settles which is ready. Since my field is trade, I note that the China-shock evidence on local labour markets is credible, while aggregate and welfare conclusions need a general-equilibrium structure that this ballot does not credit. That is part of why I do not prefer B038. I have therefore moved B038 into my alternatives in place of B020. If the committee turns to it, I would accept the three-name labour-demand version as defensible, and I would want the citation to name the empirical contribution and not claim the whole task framework.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B044 first. She says B038 is important but its credit boundary is blurred by Acemoglu and Dorn, while B044 has a more singular originating contribution. She also asks whether Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, or Redding, should be credited.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of the credit boundaries and with your point that the trade-shock weakness is not the same as the B044 weakness. I would qualify one point. Of the omitted names, Eaton-Kortum is the least substitutable for Melitz, because it builds a different, Ricardian model, so widening the group would not mainly be about them. The Bernard-Jensen empirical contribution is the closer case, and I think the committee should acknowledge that a two-name award cannot recognise it. I also accept your point that the dependence of welfare magnitudes on structural assumptions is an ordinary limit of structural work and not a flaw in the mechanism. I would not add Redding, since his strongest contributions apply and extend the framework.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B044 first with Helpman and Melitz. She would define the award as the theoretical framework of selection and reallocation, separates the well-confirmed qualitative mechanism from model-dependent welfare magnitudes, and says she would support B038 if the committee finds a convincing way to credit Dorn.
responses.response: I agree on the definition of the award and on separating mechanism from magnitudes, which is also how I now word the citation. Your conditional support for B038 shows that attribution, not importance, is what divides B038 from B044. I cannot offer a principled way to credit Dorn within a three-name cap. If the strands are split, Boppart's view that Dorn should displace Katz is coherent, and a trade-shock trio of Autor, Dorn and Hanson is the version closest to my own field. I would still not prefer it over B044, because I think the China-shock persistence debate is less settled than the firm-heterogeneity predictions.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats Bernard, Jensen, Eaton or Kortum, or Redding, as needing credit, which a two-name award cannot accommodate.
How much weight the model-dependence of welfare magnitudes (Pareto, CES) should carry compared with the well-confirmed qualitative selection mechanism.
Whether the 2008 trade prize should lower the appetite for another trade award. I think not unless the discovery overlaps, but others weigh it differently.

Which fallback I would prefer if B044 does not reach six votes, B037 for its clean attribution or B038 for its broader empirical footprint. I have not settled this order. If B038 is chosen, I would want the committee to decide whether Katz or Dorn takes the third place.
I have not independently verified citation, impact or priority claims. My assessment rests on my own knowledge of the literature and on colleagues' statements.
statement.conflict_note: Updated from round 1. My research in industrial organisation and international trade is close to B044. I disclose this as field proximity and not as evidence of merit, and I apply the same criteria as for other fields. B020 is no longer one of my alternatives. I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen. It is unrelated to any shortlisted candidate, and Hassler's preference for B037 is one of the positions I answer above. My profile documents no personal, institutional or co-authorship connection to Melitz, Helpman, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn. My spouse's public political role is noted as a public fact only and has no apparent bearing. These items are disclosed, not adjudicated, and no recusal appears needed on the supplied profile.
